gen-gf-euphoria-script-fs-public-sans: Relaxed handwriting leads in Euphoria Script, its letters tucked close with only a small step up to the capitals. And Public Sans backs it with a hefty, trustworthy body whose broad openings keep every line easy to take in.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-fs-supreme: Euphoria Script writes thin, unvarying strokes in a casual pen-and-paper hand, graceful and loosely tucked together. Supreme sets a dense, heavy-looking strip of text beneath it, and that weight gap is the draw.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-general-sans: General Sans reads crisp and smooth, its tall lowercase filling the line and every curve running without a snag. Euphoria Script sits above it as the loose handwritten voice, so the page gets some warmth first and tidy order after.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-manrope: Graceful and relaxed, Euphoria Script looks handwritten. Its best work is big and brief, a few words where those close-set pen letters can show off, while Manrope stays bright and open underneath.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-satoshi: Satoshi reads approachable, with a soaring lowercase and an e that never pinches shut. But Euphoria Script is the one for graceful, handwritten flourish, while Satoshi does the plainer job of staying legible in short bursts.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-switzer: Close-fitting handwritten letters give Euphoria Script its relaxed, pen-and-paper charm, with barely any step between lowercase and capitals. And Switzer answers that looseness with wiry, tall-waisted forms, so the handwritten warmth meets a distinctly Swiss tidiness.
gen-gf-euphoria-script-work-sans: Work Sans brings a modern, contemporary body with a high mean line and tips that never crowd together. And Euphoria Script's handwritten grace is the real contrast.
gen-gf-ewert-fs-paquito: Ewert stretches its word shapes out wide, with hairline-thin openings and only a faint thick-thin shift. Paquito follows in a confident, friendly serif, and its small drop from caps to lowercase keeps paragraphs feeling compact.
gen-gf-expletus-sans-fs-rowan: Expletus Sans is distinctive and commanding, drawn plain and sturdy with almost no variation in its strokes. But Rowan brings a literary, friendly classic serif whose thick and thin strokes make the real difference.
gen-gf-farsan-fs-rowan: Chunky, rounded and loud, Farsan has no hairlines anywhere, and its letters crowd close together. Yet Rowan does the gentler work, with literary, friendly curves and a clear gap between its thick and thin strokes.
